name: Shortcut rain
what: Keyboard keycaps with labels (Ctrl, C, V, Shift, Enter...) rain down behind you, tumbling as they fall, and land at the bottom of the frame with a bounce, piling on the ones before; at the end the pile drops away. The Editor puts them behind the person.
origin: MotionLab's own build after a design in Vibha Ramprakash's claude-video-effects (MIT), 2026-10-28
motion: three keys are already falling at f0, the rest start one after another until ~2.3 s before the end (seeded, spread over the width); each speeds up (accelerating) to a steady fall of 44-56 px a frame, spinning 2.5-7 degrees a frame and wobbling in depth; it lands on the bottom of the frame or on the highest key under it, bounces (8 f, then a small 5 f one) and turns to rest the nearest way round (9 f, decelerating); the last 11 f the pile drops away through the floor and fades (accelerating).

tracks.name: rain
tracks.easing: accelerating (slow start) to a steady fall

tracks.name: landings
tracks.what: the keys land with a bounce and pile up

tracks.name: drop away
tracks.what: the pile drops through the floor and fades

min_why: the last key has to land before the pile drops away
